study type: population cohort study with a before-and-after design
cohort: Nearly 550,000 women from 24 hospitals (8 laborist and 16 nonlaborist hospitals)
finding: Implementation of the laborist model was associated with a significant reduction in labor induction rate and preterm birth rate without adversely affecting other outcomes.
mod_finding: The implementation of a laborist model was associated with a reduction in labor induction rates and preterm birth rates but did not impact cesarean delivery rates.
